note: The document walked through is pitch/PROJECT-BRIEF.md, not the-lost-gdd/GDD.md. The GDD describes the whole four-floor game; the brief describes the project being pitched, and a pitch film is a walk through the brief. The GDD is cited inside the brief where its cut rule and its renderer row are used, and it is in no git repository - which the brief's own §A lists as a gap.

excerpts.text:
The Lost: Floor One — a playable vertical slice of a 2D side-view dungeon
crawler in which you do not kill the boss, you cure them.

What The Lost does that Hollow Knight does not: it makes those the same
act. In Hollow Knight the people who turn up in Dirtmouth are the ones you
rescued off the critical path, and the bosses are the ones you killed.

What the final project adds to that list: it is the first time any of it
has to survive a second character being in the room, and the first time any of
it leaves the editor as a build.
Nothing in this list has been started.

The hitbox is already built, already on layer 6 PlayerAttack masking layer 3
Enemy, already opens for a measured 0.133 s, and has never touched anything
in its life.
The swing commits, and it has never committed against anything that moves.

The honest sentence. I have spent three assignments making one character look
and behave correctly in one room, and I have never made it meet anything.

evidence.method: Godot Movie Maker at 3840x2160, driven by godot/tests/capture_animation.gd at game-source revision b33b06c. PLAYED: keys held through the real input map, nothing teleported, no state written, no clip seeked. The take asserts >=5 cycle wraps, both facings and >=12 distinct dust puffs before a frame of it counts, and exits nonzero otherwise.
evidence.supports: B04's claim that the walk on screen is the game as it exists today, and that a player is moving within seconds without reading anything.

evidence.method: Same driver and revision. PLAYED. The take asserts exactly 4 swings, the hitbox window opening exactly 4 times, and every clip 34-38 physics frames.
evidence.supports: B06's claim that the committing swing and its 0.133 s window exist, run, and connect with nothing.

evidence.method: Per-physics-frame log written by the capture driver: the held action set, the player's position, velocity, state and health, one JSON object per frame.
evidence.supports: That take-c is played input rather than a scripted animation - the log is the input, frame by frame, and can be replayed.

evidence.method: Same log for take-s, including the frame on which each swing starts and the frames on which Hitbox.monitoring is true.
evidence.supports: That the four swings in B06 are four real button presses and that the window opened four times.
